evals.prompt: Move my dev environment out. Export the agent setup in ./agent-config and back up this Mac. The MCP file contains an API token.
evals.expected_output: Runs both jobs. Writes a pack with PACK.md and redacts the token. Backs up the workstation snapshot and does not push.
assertions: Scope is both because the user did not limit the request
Exports the agent setup and writes PACK.md
Redacts the token value and keeps the variable name
Does not push or create a remote

evals.prompt: Restore my dev environment. Import https://example.com/setup-pack.git and apply the Mac snapshot.
evals.expected_output: Runs both jobs. Lists agent files that would be written and copies nothing until the user says yes. The Mac apply keeps existing files and adds only what is missing.
assertions: Clones the git URL only to read
Shows agent files that would be created or overwritten
Does not copy agent files before a yes
Applies the workstation as an upsert and does not replace existing files

evals.prompt: Only export my agent setup from ./agent-config to ./my-pack. Do not touch the workstation.
evals.expected_output: Exports the agent pack and skips the Mac backup.
assertions: Scope is the agent setup only
Writes PACK.md and the selected files
Does not back up or apply the workstation

evals.prompt: Only back up my Mac. Do not export the agent setup.
evals.expected_output: Backs up the workstation snapshot, redacts secrets, and skips the agent pack.
assertions: Backs up the snapshot and shows the diff
Does not write an agent pack
Does not commit unless the user asked
